current_focus.domain: Merchant-owned Stripe connection from the registry Payments plugin
current_focus.summary: Implement the first local hosted Payments connection slice: merchant-owned Stripe accounts, DinkusKit-hosted service and shared merchant identity, authenticated immutable store/account binding, resumable Stripe-hosted onboarding, authoritative readiness and a fail-closed checkout binding. Verify retries, interrupted setup, account isolation and readiness regression. Preserve Stripe-only, USD-only and Commerce ownership of checkout, attempts, orders and receipts. Consume the in-progress Commerce payment binding contract without editing its worktree. Registry installation remains the delivery target; public account sign-in, live credentials, deployment and live payment activation are not authorized by this local implementation.

decisions.choice: Ship one @dinkuskit/payments EmDash plugin with a server-owned adapter registry and exactly one active provider per store. Stripe is the only implemented and supported demo provider. Future processors may be isolated adapters behind the Commerce-owned provider contract; unknown providers fail closed, with no fallback or browser selection.

decisions.choice: DinkusKit operates the hosted Stripe connection service by default, reusing the DinkusKit merchant identity used for Inventory. The merchant owns the receiving Stripe account. The service owns authenticated store-to-account bindings, Stripe onboarding links and verified readiness, and provides the hosted integration boundary for Stripe checkout and verified updates. DinkusKit accepts the service operation responsibility. Normal users do not configure infrastructure or API keys.
